description: Mitigations for fire hazards. FR clothing prevents the critical escalation (clothing ignition). Suppression systems are the dominant engineered control.

mitigations.name: fire_resistant_design
mitigations.description: Fire-resistant building materials, compartmentation, fire-rated doors/walls. Limits fire spread and gives occupants time to escape. Inherent to the structure.
mitigations.pfd_source: Design mitigation — can't be defeated. PFD reflects structural fire rating being exceeded.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Fire compartmentation limits fire to origin compartment. Effectiveness depends on fire rating (30/60/120 min) vs fire duration.

mitigations.name: sprinkler
mitigations.description: Automatic fire suppression — sprinkler heads activate at temperature threshold. Suppresses or controls fire before it can grow. NFPA 13/BS 9251.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.05. NFPA data: sprinkler reliability ~95% when maintained. Failure: system shut off for maintenance, heads painted/blocked, water supply interrupted.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: NFPA: sprinklers control or extinguish fire in ~96% of activations. Reduces fire death rate by 87% (NFPA 2021). Highly effective when operating.

mitigations.name: fr_clothing
mitigations.description: Flame-resistant clothing prevents clothing ignition — THE critical escalation boundary for fire SIF. Standard workwear (cotton/poly) melts and sustains burning. FR self-extinguishes.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.12. Failure: not worn (most common), wrong rating for exposure, damaged/contaminated (oil-soaked FR loses protection), layered with non-FR garments underneath.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Prevents the clothing ignition escalation. With FR, a flash fire produces skin burns on exposed areas only. Without FR, clothing fire produces 25-40% TBSA deep burns (Baux rule mortality).

mitigations.name: fire_detection_alarm
mitigations.description: Smoke/heat detection with audible alarm. Provides early warning for evacuation. Does not suppress the fire — enables escape.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.05. Passive engineered. Failure: detector disabled, battery dead (domestic), alarm not heard (noisy environment), occupants don't respond.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Effectiveness is enabling escape — detection time determines available safe egress time (ASET). Effective for structural fires where occupants are remote from origin.

mitigations.name: escape_route
mitigations.description: Maintained escape routes with emergency lighting, fire doors, signage. Design mitigation — routes are inherent to the building. Post-impact because they enable escape after fire starts.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.03. Design feature. Failure: routes blocked (stored materials), fire doors propped open, emergency lighting failed.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Clear escape routes enable evacuation before flashover/smoke incapacitation. Travel distance standards (BS 9999) ensure routes reach safety within available time.

mitigations.name: emergency_response_fire
mitigations.description: Professional fire service response. Suppression, search and rescue, casualty treatment. Response time is the critical variable.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.15. Dependent on response time, access, water supply, fire service availability. Rural/industrial sites may have 15+ min response.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Professional firefighters with BA can effect rescue from smoke-filled buildings. Effectiveness drops rapidly with time — flashover typically occurs 5-10 min after ignition.
